prompt: Fatima thinks of a positive integer, adds 3 to it, squares the result and then subtracts 6. If she ends up with 43, then what number did she think of?

solutions.title: Work backwards
solutions.body:
Adding 6 to 43 gives 49; its positive square root is 7; subtracting 3 gives 4.

**Answer: 4**

prompt: Determine the value of $x$ in degrees. (The eight angles around the point are $x,2x,3x,\dots,8x$.)

solutions.title: Angles round a point
solutions.body:
The angles around a point sum to $360^\circ$: $x+2x+\cdots+8x=36x=360$, so $x=10$.

**Answer: 10**

prompt: Five consecutive numbers add up to 140. What is the smallest number?

solutions.title: Middle number
solutions.body:
The middle number is the average, $140\div5=28$. The numbers are 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, so the smallest is 26.

**Answer: 26**

prompt: Determine the size of the angle marked $x$ in degrees.

solutions.title: Angle sum of the quadrilateral
solutions.body:
The figure is a quadrilateral (arrowhead) with interior angles $80^\circ$, $30^\circ$, $20^\circ$ and a reflex angle at the dent equal to $360^\circ-x$. The interior angles sum to $360^\circ$: $80+30+20+(360-x)=360$, so $x=130$.

**Answer: 130**

solutions.title: Construction line
solutions.body:
Extend the segment that ends at the dent until it meets the opposite side. By the exterior angle theorem the two angles it makes add up to $80^\circ+30^\circ+20^\circ=130^\circ$, and this equals $x$.

**Answer: 130**

prompt: Find the value of $n$ if $n$ is a whole number and $\frac1n$ is greater than $\frac13$ but less than $\frac34$.

solutions.title: Common denominator
solutions.body:
$\frac13<\frac1n<\frac34$ means $\frac43<n<3$, so $n=2$.

**Answer: 2**

prompt: The diagram shows a large square subdivided into nine identical smaller squares. If the large square has an area of $81\text{ cm}^2$, what is the area of the shaded region in $\text{cm}^2$?

solutions.title: Subtract unshaded triangles
solutions.body:
The large square has side 9, each small square has side 3. The three unshaded triangles have areas $\frac12\cdot9\cdot3=13.5$, $\frac12\cdot6\cdot6=18$ and $\frac12\cdot3\cdot3=4.5$, total 36. Shaded area $=81-36=45$.

**Answer: 45**

prompt: A 2 m long snake enters a 2 m long pipe. The snake moves at a constant speed of $0{,}2$ m/s (that is, $0.2$ m/s). How many seconds will it take for the snake to enter the pipe and then fully exit the pipe on the other side?

solutions.title: Distance
solutions.body:
The tail of the snake must travel the length of the pipe plus the length of the snake: $2+2=4$ m. Time $=4\div0.2=20$ s.

**Answer: 20**

prompt: On the number line shown, the ratio AB:BC is 5:3. What number is located at B?
The average of ten numbers is 15. If the four largest numbers are 20, 22, 23 and 25, what is the average of the six smallest numbers?

solutions.title: Totals
solutions.body:
The ten numbers sum to 150. The four largest sum to 90. The six smallest sum to 60, average 10.

**Answer: 10**

prompt: A bus completed 3 trips. On the first trip it was 30% full. On its second trip it was 90% full, and on its third trip it was 60% full. If in total 72 different bus tickets were used, what is the capacity of the bus?
Determine the size of the unknown angle in degrees. (The two long horizontal lines are parallel.)

solutions.title: Follow the directions
solutions.body:
Measure directions of the line segments from the horizontal. The first slanted segment makes $60^\circ$ with the horizontal (since the interior angle is $120^\circ$, its supplement is $60^\circ$). At the $90^\circ$ turn the next segment descends at $30^\circ$ below the horizontal. At the $70^\circ$ valley the last segment rises at $80^\circ$ above the horizontal ($30+70=100$ turned back, giving $80^\circ$). At the top the unknown angle is between this segment and the horizontal line to the right: it is $180-80=100^\circ$.

**Answer: 100**

prompt:
Given the following pattern, in which row will the number 2024 lie?

| Row | Numbers |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2, 3, 4 |
| 3 | 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 |
| 4 | 10, 11, ..., 16 |
| 5 | 17, 18, ..., 25 |

solutions.title: Last number of each row
solutions.body:
Row $k$ ends with $k^2$ (1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...), and has $2k-1$ numbers. $44^2=1936$ and $45^2=2025$, so 2024 is in row 45.

**Answer: 45**

prompt: How many whole numbers from 1 to 500 are divisible by both 3 and 5?

solutions.title: Multiples of 15
solutions.body:
The numbers are multiples of 15: $15,30,\dots,495$. Since $\lfloor500/15\rfloor=33$, there are 33.

**Answer: 33**

prompt: Tom and Dick together weigh 135 kg. Tom and Harry together weigh 140 kg. Dick and Harry together weigh 125 kg. How many kilograms does Harry weigh?

solutions.title: Add all three
solutions.body:
Adding gives twice the total: $135+140+125=400$, so all three weigh 200 kg. Harry $=200-135=65$.

**Answer: 65**

prompt: 36 identical cubes are used to build a rectangular prism. One such example is shown. How many other rectangular prisms (with different dimensions) can be made using all 36 cubes?

solutions.title: List factorisations
solutions.body:
The dimensions $a\le b\le c$ with $abc=36$ are: $1\times1\times36$, $1\times2\times18$, $1\times3\times12$, $1\times4\times9$, $1\times6\times6$, $2\times2\times9$, $2\times3\times6$, $3\times3\times4$. That is 8; the one shown is $3\times3\times4$, so there are 7 others.

**Answer: 7**

prompt: Josh and Thabo are at the same starting point on a long straight road. Josh starts driving at a constant speed of 70 km/h. One hour later, Thabo starts driving at a constant speed of 84 km/h in the same direction as Josh. How many hours will it take Thabo to catch up with Josh?

solutions.title: Closing the gap
solutions.body:
When Thabo starts, Josh is 70 km ahead. Thabo gains $84-70=14$ km every hour, so it takes $70\div14=5$ hours.

**Answer: 5**

prompt: There are only red and blue marbles in a jar. At the beginning, the ratio of red to blue marbles is 4:3. One blue marble is then removed and replaced with a red marble. This changes the ratio of red to blue marbles to 3:2. How many red marbles were there originally in the jar?

solutions.title: Total stays the same
solutions.body:
The total number of marbles is unchanged. It is a multiple of $4+3=7$ and of $3+2=5$, hence of 35. With 35 marbles: 20 red and 15 blue originally; after the swap 21 and 14, ratio $3:2$. With 70 marbles the swap would need 2 marbles to change colour, not 1. So the original number of red marbles is 20.

**Answer: 20**

solutions.title: Algebra
solutions.body:
Let there be $4k$ red and $3k$ blue. Then $\frac{4k+1}{3k-1}=\frac32$, so $8k+2=9k-3$ and $k=5$. Red: $4k=20$.

**Answer: 20**

prompt: The surface area of a large cube is $864\text{ cm}^2$. This cube is cut into $n$ identical smaller cubes each with a surface area of $54\text{ cm}^2$. How many smaller cubes are there?

solutions.title: Side lengths
solutions.body:
Large cube: face area $144$, side 12. Small cube: face area $9$, side 3. The number of small cubes is $(12/3)^3=4^3=64$.

**Answer: 64**

prompt: The diagram shows three squares. Find the total shaded area.

solutions.title: Find the sides
solutions.body:
Let the smallest square have side $x$. The middle square is 8 larger in side: $x+8$. The left square is $3$ shorter than the middle: $x+5$. The widths add up to 25: $(x+5)+(x+8)+x=25$, so $x=4$. The sides are 9, 12 and 4, and the total area is $81+144+16=241$.

**Answer: 241**

prompt: Neo begins with the set of numbers from 1 to 10. After removing one of these numbers, she places each of the other numbers in one of two sets. The product of the numbers in one of these sets equals the product of the numbers in the other set. Which number did Neo remove?

solutions.title: Prime 7
solutions.body:
The prime 7 divides exactly one of the numbers 1 to 10, namely 7 itself. If 7 were placed in one of the sets, the product of the other set could not contain a factor 7 and the products would differ. So 7 must be removed. Indeed $1\cdot2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot6=720=8\cdot9\cdot10$.

**Answer: 7**

prompt: A donkey is tied to rope AB of length 3 m. The rope is connected to a metal rod CD, of length 12 m. The metal rod is fixed at ground level, but the rope can slide freely along the rod. If the total possible area which the donkey can graze is $a\pi+b$, find the value of $a+b$.

solutions.title: Shape of the grazing region
solutions.body:
The donkey can reach every point within 3 m of the rod: a rectangle $12\times6$ (3 m on each side of the rod) and two half-discs of radius 3 at the ends, which together form one full disc of area $9\pi$. Total area $72+9\pi$, so $a=9$, $b=72$ and $a+b=81$.

**Answer: 81**

prompt: In the diagram, $AC\perp BD$, $ED\parallel AC$ and $AE\perp AB$. $\hat B=45^\circ$ and $DE=6$. If the area of triangle ABC is 25, determine the area of trapezium ACDE.

solutions.title: Extend to a triangle
solutions.body:
Extend BD and AE to meet at F. Triangle ABF has a right angle at A and $45^\circ$ at B, so it is isosceles right, and its altitude AC bisects it into two congruent right triangles ABC and ACF, each of area 25. Since $ED\parallel AC$, triangle DEF is right-angled at D with angle $45^\circ$ at F, so $DF=DE=6$ and its area is $18$. The trapezium ACDE is triangle ACF minus triangle DEF: $25-18=7$.

**Answer: 7**

prompt: A large rectangle ABCD is split into two smaller rectangles. The areas of these two smaller rectangles are $40\text{ cm}^2$ and $60\text{ cm}^2$. If the side lengths of rectangle ABCD are integer values, determine the smallest possible perimeter of ABCD.

solutions.title: Common height
solutions.body:
The two small rectangles share a side $h$ (the height of ABCD), which divides both 40 and 60, so $h\in\{1,2,4,5,10,20\}$. The width is $\frac{40+60}{h}=\frac{100}{h}$ and the perimeter is $2\left(h+\frac{100}h\right)$. This is smallest for $h=10$: $2(10+10)=40$.

**Answer: 40**

prompt: Kamohelo finds the sum of the two digits of a 2-digit number, as well as the product of the two digits. She then adds the sum to the product and realizes that the result equals the 2-digit number itself. For how many 2-digit numbers will this be the case?

solutions.title: Digit equation
solutions.body:
For $10A+B$: $(A+B)+AB=10A+B$ gives $AB=9A$, so $B=9$. The numbers are 19, 29, ..., 99: nine numbers.

**Answer: 9**

prompt:
There are five cards in a bag. Each card has a whole number on it. Whenever three of these cards are chosen at random we find the following probabilities:
- The probability is $P\%$ that the sum is equal to 14;
- The probability is $(100-P)\%$ that the sum is equal to 15.

Find the value of $P$.

solutions.title: Which cards
solutions.body:
Only two different sums occur, so the cards cannot carry three different numbers, nor a split of three equal and two equal (that gives three sums). So four cards carry $x$ and one card carries $y$; the sums are $3x$ and $2x+y$. As 15 is divisible by 3 but 14 is not, $x=5$ and $y=4$. Of the 10 possible triples, 6 contain the 4-card (sum 14). So $P=60$.

**Answer: 60**
